problem.text: The supplied engine description is a proposed design; no implementation exists.

desired_change.text: Build a custom inference engine for Meta Muse Spark Open that runs on NVIDIA DGX Spark.

requested_result.text: An implemented engine conforming to the attached System Ontology descriptions of the model, machine, evaluation target, whole engine and engine nodes, including the target's required delivery artifacts.

context.name: Attached System Ontology files
context.role: The user supplies these descriptions as the statement of what is wanted.

context.name: Target specification
context.role: Distinguishes required scope from proposed bench settings and project decisions left UNSET; current bench practice is explicitly not itself a project requirement.

context.name: Muse Spark Open UD-IQ2_XXS model description
context.role: Describes the third-party conversion used by the bench, its structure and stored tensor sizes; using this lower precision changes outputs and has not been allowed or refused by the target.

context.name: NVIDIA DGX Spark hardware description
context.role: Specifies the 128 GB configuration, with CPU and GPU accessing a unified memory pool and storage supplying data to that pool.

context.name: Proposed whole-engine design
context.role: Supplies a design derived from Strata and ds4, rather than evidence of a built engine.

context.name: Proposed node-level description
context.role: Supplies component responsibilities and recorded design choices. Node-type fit and reason annotations describe classification limitations rather than new user instructions.

in_scope.text: Implement the supplied whole-engine and node-level descriptions as the user's requested engine.

The supplied design keeps weights needed by every token in memory, stores all experts on storage in contiguous expert ranges, caches frequently used experts, and overlaps missed-expert reads with computation of cached experts once routing is known.
The supplied design prepares expert ranges offline and reads prompt chunks one layer at a time so a missed expert used by multiple tokens is read once per chunk.

The supplied design includes model preparation and loading, memory sizing, layer computation, expert routing and caching, prompt and token execution, conversation-state reuse and persistence, serving, configuration, supervision and telemetry.

out_of_scope.text: The first version does not load the perception encoder for image, video or audio; its interface is text in and text out.
The supplied engine command loop runs one prompt read and one generation at a time.

constraints.text: The engine must run on NVIDIA DGX Spark.
Container packaging and text input and output are required. Service form is proposed, and the target leaves streaming UNSET.

The target defines memory accounting over everything the engine's container holds in the unified pool at any moment, including CPU and GPU process allocations and attributable file page cache; the operating system and other processes are outside that boundary. The applicable budget remains unresolved.

The node design budgets shared weights, configured-context attention state, staging and a reserve before assigning the remainder to the expert cache. It refuses startup below its minimum cache, stated as at least 8 times 62 experts.
The quality comparison and allowed model transformations are not settled. Current bench use of lower-precision weights does not establish permission for output changes or define a quality pass.

Proposed engine TTFT runs from request admission to production of the first output token and excludes model loading. Proposed decode rate excludes the first token, although the bench has not checked that convention in runtime source. Peak memory uses the container accounting boundary over the whole bench run; existing baseline measurements do not yet compute that quantity.

user_targets.target_text: Pass/fail budget unresolved: the kickoff target is a 128 GB unified-memory working set; 80 GB describes the Strata reference configuration; 12 GB is a feasibility target that the bench proposes to interpret as GPU working set. These figures must not be merged into a selected budget.
A pass/fail context-length requirement is UNSET. The bench's 20,480-token server setting and approximately 16,000-token tested prompts are explicitly not engine requirements.

Quality is proposed as pass/fail, but the deciding comparison and threshold are UNSET. The bench proposes llama.cpp with the pinned Unsloth UD-IQ2_XXS conversion, published tokenizer, greedy temperature 0 and seed 1234 as baseline. Its task-score and token-probability comparisons do not require token-by-token identity; the recorded GSM8K score of 0.94 is not a pass threshold.

These quantities are proposed for reporting, without numerical performance acceptance targets. The proposed speed workload uses an approximately 2,000-token prompt after 0, 4,000 or 16,000 tokens of earlier context, 128 output tokens, one request at a time, new prompts with prompt cache off, and up to 6 discarded warm-up requests.

uncertainties.description: The project has not confirmed the required checkpoint. The bench's Unsloth UD-IQ2_XXS conversion is proposed, while preparation descriptions refer to a published checkpoint.
uncertainties.clarification: Identify the required checkpoint and confirm whether the proposed Unsloth UD-IQ2_XXS conversion is the engine's required input.

uncertainties.description: The applicable memory budget is unresolved. The source distinguishes the 128 GB target, the 80 GB Strata reference configuration and a 12 GB feasibility target with only a proposed GPU-working-set interpretation.
uncertainties.clarification: Specify the binding memory budget, units and accounting boundary, and state whether the 12 GB feasibility figure is a separate requirement.

uncertainties.description: The target's 128 GB working-set figure exceeds the approximately 127 GB the supplied target text says is allocatable on the machine. The project has not resolved how that figure is to apply.
uncertainties.clarification: Resolve the stated 128 GB working-set target against the supplied machine's allocatable memory and the required reserve.

uncertainties.description: The pass/fail context length is UNSET; neither model capacity nor the bench's own configuration defines the engine requirement.
uncertainties.clarification: Specify the context length the engine must support for acceptance.

uncertainties.description: The quality pass rule and threshold are undefined. Available bench comparisons include task-score change relative to run noise and top-1 agreement or KL divergence, without selecting the deciding rule.
uncertainties.clarification: Confirm the quality baseline and task set, select the deciding comparison or comparisons, and specify their pass thresholds.

uncertainties.description: Allowed transformations relative to the baseline are UNSET, including whether output changes from lower-precision weights are permitted.
uncertainties.clarification: Specify which model or numerical transformations the engine may make relative to the confirmed baseline.

uncertainties.description: The evaluation workload and measurement definitions are marked proposed bench practice rather than confirmed project requirements.
uncertainties.clarification: Confirm or replace the proposed speed workload, quality task set, TTFT definition, decode first-token convention and peak-memory measurement procedure.

uncertainties.description: Service form is proposed and streaming is UNSET. The proposed serving design supports response delivery during generation or at completion, but the required interface behavior is not selected.
uncertainties.clarification: Confirm the required service interface and whether streaming is required, optional or excluded.

uncertainties.description: The whole-engine summary says expert weights are about three times machine memory, while the current conversion description reports 205.96 GB of expert weights for the nominal 128 GB machine. The system description separately associates roughly 399.43 GB with published 4-bit expert weights.
uncertainties.clarification: Resolve which weight representation governs the engine design and its resource assumptions, and correct the incompatible size narrative accordingly.

readiness.reason: The requested engine and hardware are identified, but checkpoint selection, memory feasibility and budget, required context length, quality acceptance, permitted transformations, evaluation definitions and interface behavior remain unresolved; supplied descriptions also contain incompatible weight-size assumptions.
